subject: Urgent: stepwise performance degradation after variant ramp (p95/p99 spikes)
messages:
From: Sarah Emerson <sarah.emerson@quantify.ai>
To: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: model variant rollout — seeing p95/p99 jumps

Hi Mina,

We started seeing an uptick in tail latency across several production routes after you ramped a new serving variant yesterday evening. p95 for our chat endpoint climbed from ~120ms to ~420ms and p99 spiked to over 1.6s. This started appearing around 22:10 PDT on Aug 28 and has been intermittently worse during our peak bursts.

Attached is a screenshot from our monitoring showing the stepwise jumps (perf-dash-20270829.png). We don't have a full root cause yet — our initial look shows increased async queue depth and a small rise in 5xx errors (0.3% to 1.1%). Can you confirm if any variant was rolled to our traffic cohort between 20:00–23:30 PDT? This is impacting a live feature for several key customers.

Thanks,
Sarah Emerson
Head of Platform Operations, Quantify AI
attachments: perf-dash-20270829.png
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Emerson <sarah.emerson@quantify.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: model variant rollout — seeing p95/p99 jumps

Sarah — thank you for the signal and the screenshot.

We rolled variant v3b into your canary cohort at ~20:15 PDT yesterday with a 15% traffic allocation as part of the staged rollout. I’ve looped in Dev (serving runtime) and Marissa (customer ops) to triage immediately.

Immediate actions we plan to take:
- Pause further ramping and hold allocation at 15% (already triggered).
- Run quick profiling on the v3b nodes and compare KV cache hit/eviction rates vs v3a.
- If the regression reproduces on our side we will roll back the variant in your cohort and open an incident timeline for you.

Can you confirm: are you observing increased payload sizes or longer user messages around the times of the spikes? Any recent prompt/template changes on your end?

I’ll update you within 45 minutes with initial findings.

— Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: model variant rollout — seeing p95/p99 jumps

Team — quick summary from the runtime profiling run (10:00–10:02 PDT):
- v3b shows a ~3.2x increase in tail generation time for sequences > 400 tokens vs v3a under identical requests.
- Observed KV cache churn: v3b's tokenization changes increase the effective cache key variety resulting in higher cache miss rates (miss rate up from 6% to 21%).
- During spikes we see GPU context switch latency increase and a higher probability of small batching inefficiencies (many single-request batches).
- Error rate uptick is correlated with transient OOM retries on some 1/20 pods which then push requests to colder pods causing queueing and increased p99.

Immediate recommendation: pause the canary roll (already consented by Mina), revert your canary cohort to v3a for Quantify AI, and trigger an in-depth profiling job to instrument tokenizer outputs and cache key distribution.

I can run the rollback now if we get approval from Ops/CS. Also recommend we prep a brief exec note for Sales/Customer Success since this impacts a key customer SLA.

Attachments: profiling-log-v3b.txt (sample traces)

— Dev
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
